incidents.cause: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff, which resulted in a runway excursion and impact with a fence.
The pilot’s failure to obtain a proper touchdown point while attempting to land on a very short and rough turf runway, which resulted in a runway overrun and collision with vegetation and terrain.
The pilot's loss of directional control during a precautionary off-field landing that he performed after encountering deteriorating weather conditions.
The pilot's inadequate compensation for the crosswind condition and failure to maintain directional control.
A loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
The pilot’s failure to maintain directional control while landing on a wet grass strip.
The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed which caused the airplane to exceed its critical angle of attack and led to an aerodynamic stall.

The pilot's inadequate preflight planning, which resulted in an attempted takeoff over the airplane's maximum gross weight and beyond its aft center of gravity limit. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of total flight experience in the aircraft make and model.

The pilot’s failure to maintain an adequate airspeed during a go-around, which resulted in a loss of airplane control. Contributing to the accident was the inadvertent activation of the fuel boost pump during the attempted go-around.
The pilot’s failure to abort the takeoff after the partial loss of engine power before liftoff, and the partial loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.

The airplane’s encounter with a strong tailwind and/or windshear, which resulted in an inadvertent stall. Contributing to the accident was the pilot’s continuation of the unstable approach, long landing, and delayed decision to conduct a go-around.

The loss of engine power due to fuel starvation for reasons that could not be determined because a postaccident examination of the airframe and engine did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
The fueler's falling asleep in the fueling truck with the truck in neutral and without the parking brake set, which allowed the truck to roll until it impacted the airplane.
The flight attendant’s use of improper procedures when opening the main cabin door.

The Start Operability Bleed Valve (OBV) fuel return adapter-fitting fractured and separated in cyclic fatigue, which allowed fuel to spill onto a hot engine case that ignited the undercowl fire.  The OBV fuel adapter-fitting was dropped and the damage reduced its load carrying and fatigue capability
The pilot's failure to attain the proper touchdown point and exceedance of the target touchdown speed, which resulted in a runway overrun.
A manufacturing defect that resulted in fatigue failure of the left main landing gear trunnion.
The pilot landed without lowering the landing gear. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to fly the airplane with an inoperative wing flap system.
A total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation as the result of a degraded fuel primer check valve.
A collision with trees during takeoff for reasons that could not be determined based on available information.
The pilot’s failure to maintain control of the airplane on takeoff for unknown reasons.
The noncertificated pilot's failure to maintain airplane control, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of flight experience and qualification.
A steep descent and impact with terrain during final approach for reasons that could not be determined.
The separation and subsequent ingestion of the fenestron fairing cover into the fenestron blades for undetermined reasons.
The pilot’s improper decision to review an aircraft logbook while enroute, which resulted in controlled flight into terrain.
